# MM-P3-L3-CN02 Maintenance manual - Machining CNC turning center #2

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3, line P3-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L3-CN02

Scope
This document provides maintenance instructions for Machining CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P3-L3-CN02). It covers routine mechanical checks, chuck jaw bolt verification, spindle warm-up procedure prior to production, and required records. This manual is intended for qualified maintenance personnel and machine operators performing routine preventive maintenance and pre-production checks. Reference related procedural and safety requirements in MM-P3-L3-CN02-S1, SOP-P3-L3-02, and SOP-P3-L3-04.

Tools
Required items for the procedures that follow: calibrated torque wrench capable of applying the chuck jaw bolt torque specified below, basic hand tools, cleaning supplies appropriate for machine tool environments, lint-free shop cloths, manufacturer-approved lubricants and grease guns as called out in equipment manufacturer guidance, and the machine control pendant for executing spindle warm-up cycles. Ensure the torque wrench calibration certificate is available per traceability practice.

Procedure
Background and rationale
Proper clamping of workpieces and stable spindle operation are critical to part accuracy and operator safety. The chuck jaw bolts secure the jaws to the chuck body; incorrect bolt preload can lead to jaw loosening, runout, and component damage. The spindle assembly requires a controlled warm-up to achieve stable thermal conditions, which reduces dimensional drift during the initial production run.

Preparation
Verify machine is in a safe state for maintenance per SOP-P3-L3-02 and SOP-P3-L3-04. Lockout and tagout the machine as required by site practice before performing mechanical adjustments when exposed rotating elements are involved. Confirm presence of required tools and torque wrench calibration documentation. Consult MM-P3-L3-CN02-S1 for any model-specific notes.

Chuck jaw bolt torque verification
Inspect the chuck and jaws visually for debris, visible damage, or abnormal wear. Clean the mating surfaces of the jaw and chuck using an appropriate solvent and cloth. Seat the jaw on the chuck and hand-thread the jaw bolts to ensure proper engagement.

Set the calibrated torque wrench to the specified value and apply torque to each chuck jaw bolt in a cross-pattern sequence to achieve even preload. The chuck jaw bolt torque for Machining CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P3-L3-CN02) is 75 N·m. After completing the torque sequence, perform a second pass to verify bolts remain at the specified torque.

Rationale: Applying the specified torque ensures consistent clamping force and prevents loosening during operation. Using a cross pattern equalizes load and minimizes distortion of the chuck face.

Spindle warm-up
Prior to loading hardened work material or beginning critical production, perform the spindle warm-up routine with the machine in run-permit state. Activate the spindle warm-up cycle using the control pendant and monitor spindle behavior throughout the sequence. The spindle warm-up time for Machining CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P3-L3-CN02) is 24 minutes.

Rationale: Gradual thermal stabilization of spindle bearings and spindle headstock reduces dimensional drift and runout, improving first-piece accuracy and prolonging bearing life.

Examples and special cases
If a jaw bolt fails to reach the specified torque without evidence of thread strip or damage, remove the bolt and inspect threads and mating insert. Replace damaged hardware using manufacturer-approved parts and re-torque. If the spindle exhibits abnormal vibration, noise, or temperature behavior during warm-up, stop the warm-up routine and escalate to maintenance diagnostics per SOP-P3-L3-04. Record observations and any corrective actions taken.

Records to keep
Maintain a maintenance log entry for each completed chuck torque verification and each spindle warm-up event. The log entry should include the equipment id, date, personnel performing the action, confirmation that the chuck jaw bolt torque was set to 75 N·m, confirmation that the spindle warm-up was completed for 24 minutes, and any anomalies or corrective actions. Retain torque wrench calibration records with the maintenance log per document control practice. If parts are replaced, reference MM-P3-L3-CN02-S1 for part identification and record supplier lot or traceability per site requirements.

Acceptance criteria
Acceptance is achieved when the following conditions are met: all chuck jaw bolts are torqued to the specified value and hold after verification; the spindle warm-up sequence completes without abnormal vibration or audible distress and is completed for the specified duration; no visible damage or contamination remains on the chuck mating surfaces; and entries in the maintenance log are complete and legible, including notation of the applied chuck jaw bolt torque and spindle warm-up time as stated.

Nonconformance and corrective action
If any condition fails to meet acceptance criteria, cease production and follow escalation procedures in SOP-P3-L3-04. Tag the machine out of service until corrective actions are documented and verified. Document all corrective steps in the maintenance log and reference MM-P3-L3-CN02-S1 for replacement part guidance.

Related documents
MM-P3-L3-CN02-S1  
SOP-P3-L3-02  
SOP-P3-L3-04

Revision history and approvals
Revision control and approval signatures are maintained in the document control system. Store completed maintenance logs and torque calibration records alongside this manual entry in the equipment folder for EQ-P3-L3-CN02.
